description: Relay reads (SPEC.md §13). Complete reads: the leases of deposit addresses are read with "limit": 100, page after page, until a page is not full. `cases`: what one relay answers to each page the read asks, in order (`pages`): its events, each as `[id, created_at]` as the relay wrote them (`created_at` may be anything), or "fails" (the page fails: a timeout, a closed connection, a CLOSED). The next page is asked with `until` the oldest `created_at` of the last page's events with a string `id` and a safe integer `created_at` (an `id` that is not a string, null here, is no event of the read). `expected`: `untils`, the `until` of each page the read asks (null: the first page, without `until`); `answered`, whether the relay answered (its first page did not fail); `complete`, whether its read is complete; `kept`, how many events it keeps (once per id, from every page). `lists`: whether a read over a list of relays is complete, from what each relay's read was ("complete", "incomplete" or "failed"): when a majority of the list read completely. `paged`: paged reads (a sale's declarations), at most `pages` pages, each relay's answers as in `cases` (the events' other members, which these pairs leave out, do not matter: an event that does not check out pages the read all the same); `expected` as in `cases`, without `complete` (`kept`: the events with a string `id` and a safe integer `created_at`, once per id). `onEveryRelay`: what a read on every relay of a list gives (SPEC.md §13, Reads on every relay), from what each relay's read was when the read went on: "complete" or "incomplete" (its read ended, complete or not; a read that is not a complete read ends one way only, and its `complete` is not read), "failed", or "reading" (still reading: it has not answered, whatever pages it sent). `expected`: whether a majority answered (`answered`; else the read is `network`), and whether a majority read completely (`complete`). A complete read on every relay does not go on while a relay still reading could still make a majority read completely (it waits for that relay, one `relayTimeoutMs` at most): a case where such a relay is "reading" ("complete", "incomplete", "reading", for one) tests the count alone. End to end, that relay is one that fails at its timeout, and the expected result is the same: a relay still reading has neither answered nor read completely.

cases.name: 99 events: complete at the first page
100 events, then none older: complete at the second page, asked until the oldest second
a second holding more events than a page: incomplete
a second split over two pages: complete
a full page without a safe integer created_at: incomplete
a full page with some created_at beyond 2^53: the next until from the others
a full page whose oldest created_at is a string: until from the others
a full page whose new events are undated, the dated one seen before: the next page from it
a page of more than 100 events: the limit ignored, incomplete
the first page fails: the relay failed
a page fails after the first: incomplete
20 full pages: incomplete, the 21st never asked
19 full pages, then one of 50: complete at the 20th
a full page whose oldest created_at is an event's without a string id: until from the others
a page holding an id twice: kept once

paged.name: an empty first page: one page
events, then an empty page: the next page until the oldest second
the oldest second wherever it is in the page
a page with nothing new: the next page one second earlier
new events in the oldest second: that second asked again
an id that is not a string: it neither pages the read nor is kept
a created_at beyond 2^53, or in a string: it neither pages the read nor is kept
a page without an event dated by a safe integer: the read ends there
a new undated event and dated ones seen before: the next page one second earlier
an id twice in a page: kept once
the first page fails: the relay failed
a page fails after the first: what was read is kept
20 pages at most: the 21st is never asked

onEveryRelay.name: a majority read completely, one still reading
two reads ended, one complete, one still reading: answered, not complete
one read ended, two still reading: fewer than a majority answered
one read ended, one failed, one still reading: fewer than a majority answered
five relays, three reads ended: a majority answered
five relays, two reads complete, three still reading
two relays, one still reading: the majority of two is two
one relay, its read ended incomplete
